title: The record of a run
description: A sketch on the frame clock, run from its first frame to its end and written into one file (`mokume run --record <path>`, `mokume watch --record <path>`). It holds what is needed to play the same run again and get the same pictures on the same machine (ADR-0045 decision 10): the state the run started from, and for every advance() the inputs, the knob writes and the timed observation that reached the frame, plus the values a replay compares against (the exposed values of every frame and a hash of the picture every 60 frames and at the end). **The file is complete only when `complete` is true.** While the run is being written it is `<path>.partial`, and `<path>` appears only when the run ended cleanly (the window closed, SIGTERM, or Control + C); a run that was killed leaves only the `.partial` file, which is not a record. A sketch on the wall clock is not recorded. `mokume watch --record` writes one record per build, a file each (`take.json` → `take-1.json`, `take-2.json`, …): a rebuild is a cut between two records. Later stages add keys (for example messages that arrive from outside, each with the frame and time it arrived), so a reader that meets a key it does not know in a record of its own `schemaVersion` skips it; the keys listed here are the whole set of this version (additionalProperties is false), so a writer that adds one updates this schema first.

schemaVersion.description: The version of this format. A reader refuses a version it does not read, and says so.

id.description: This record's identifier, made when the run starts. Something that points at the record — an observation of one frame together with the conditions it was taken under — names this id and a frame number.

clock.description: The clock the run was on. Only the frame clock is recorded, so `kind` is always `frames`.

frameRate.description: Frames per second of the clock: one draw() is exactly 1 / frameRate seconds.

size.description: The size, in pixels, of the picture the pixel hashes are taken of. A replay at another size cannot match.

start.description: The state the run started from, taken after the saved knob values were restored and before setup() ran. A replay sets it up the same way before setup().

seed.description: The state the random numbers started from. It is always 0: a run starts from the default seed, and a randomSeed() the sketch calls itself is part of the sketch.

seconds.description: The author's clock (the time the sketch sees, including a time it stopped or jumped) at the first frame, in seconds. It is not 0 for a build that `mokume watch --keep-time` carried on from the previous one: the value is the one the first frame actually started from.

paused.description: Whether the author's clock was stopped at the first frame (pauseTime()). True for a build `mokume watch --keep-time` started from a clock that was left stopped: without it a replay would start moving from the first frame.

params.description: The values of every knob the sketch declares (@Param), in the order they were declared. A value the saved state restored is included.

steps.description: One entry per advance() that delivered the inputs or drew a frame, in order. **`step` counts the advance() calls that reached the delivery of input**, and a stopped sketch (noLoop()) that nothing reached is left out, so a gap in `step` is an advance() in which nothing happened. Inputs that reached the same frame are **not merged**: each bundle belongs to its own advance(), because every delivery resets the per-frame amounts (scroll, drag), and a sketch stopped with noLoop() takes a bundle per advance().

step.description: The count of advance() calls that delivered input before this one, from 0.

frame.description: The frame number when the advance() ended: the frame it drew, or the last frame drawn when it drew none.

drew.description: Whether this advance() drew a frame. False for a stopped sketch that only took inputs.

inputs.description: The input events that reached the sketch before this advance() delivered them, **as they arrived** and in order: one event per item, in the same form as one line of the input request (`input-request.schema.json`, an item of `events`), which is also what the tool writes to a sketch's standard input. An event is kept before it is applied, so one that the sketch later drops (a move that would overflow a 32-bit float) is in here too, and a replay drops it in the same place. Omitted when none arrived.

params.description: The knob writes that came from outside (the window's knob panel, the params facet, the tool's window) before this advance(), **as the value the knob took** (after it was clamped into its range), in order. A value the sketch assigns itself is not a write from outside and is not recorded. Omitted when none came.

observe.description: This advance() drew the frame an observation at a given time asked for (`time` in the observation request).

time.description: The time in seconds the frame was drawn at.

expose.description: The values the sketch exposed with expose() on this frame, by name — what a replay compares against, frame by frame. A value measured with measure() is not here: it is a time, and differs every run. Omitted when the sketch exposed nothing.

pixelHash.description: A hash of the picture of this frame. Taken when the frame number is a multiple of 60, and only then. The last frame of the run is in `last`.

unreproducible.description: What was used that a replay cannot be promised to match, each with a reason, once per reason. A record with this key is not promised to replay frame for frame; a replay names it too. Omitted when there is nothing.

step.description: The advance() it was first noticed in or before.

reason.description: Why, in a form to show a person. `Replay is not guaranteed (non-finite input)` is an input event that came with a number that is not finite (NaN, infinity) by InputState.enqueue(_:), which the record cannot keep: the form of an event is a line of JSON, which writes such a number as 0, so a replay would apply a different event.

last.description: The last frame the run drew, and a hash of its picture. Omitted when the run drew no frame.

complete.description: The mark of a finished record. It is written last, after everything the run produced; a file without it is not a record.

pixelHash.description: SHA-256, in lowercase hex, of the bytes of the picture an outlet gets (8 bits per channel, RGBA, rows from the top, no padding) — the same picture a window shows and an observation writes. It is promised to match only on the same machine (ADR-0025 level 3).

namedValue.description: One knob and its value, written as in the params facet (`params-request.schema.json`).

value.description: The value. float and int are numbers, bool is a boolean, string is text, color is a tuple with red, green, blue and alpha (premultiplied, in the working space), and vec2 and vec3 are arrays of components.
